source_basis.title: Process Design of Oil and Gas Separators and Scrubbers
source_basis.usage_note: This library converts selected API RP 12J process-design logic into an application-oriented preliminary sizing and recommendation framework.

design_philosophy.calculation_basis: evaluate all applicable operating cases and select the governing requirement

revision_summary: Added intention, importance, sizing effect, risk and recommendation for each worked-example assumption.
Added a synthetic horizontal three-phase separator worked example.
Added calculation trace, pass/fail checks and UI recommendation messages.
No final mechanical pressure-vessel design has been added.

droplet_terminal_velocity.expression: sqrt((4 * gravity_acceleration_m_s2 * droplet_diameter_m * abs(dispersed_density_kg_m3 - continuous_density_kg_m3)) / (3 * drag_coefficient * continuous_density_kg_m3))

rules.basis: three-phase and liquid-liquid separation generally benefit from horizontal geometry
large liquid-liquid interface and separation length are normally required
compressor suction scrubbers are commonly vertical

rules.when: slug_flow_expected == true or required_slug_volume_m3 > 0 or required_surge_volume_m3 > 0

rules.basis: larger gas-liquid interfacial area and lower liquid disturbance may be advantageous

rules.when: gas_volume_fraction is high and liquid_flow_m3_s is low and plot_area_restricted == true
rules.basis: gas handling dominates and footprint is constrained
rules.note: No universal API GVF threshold is defined. Company thresholds must be configured separately.

limitations: fouling and erosion must be reviewed
small passages may be unsuitable for severe fouling or solids
not preferred for high performance service

preferred_applications: low gas volume fraction horizontal separator
limitations: not suitable for stringent carryover requirements

inlet_device_selection_rules.when: orientation == 'horizontal' and high_liquid_loading == true and separation_performance_class == 'bulk'

mist_eliminator_selection_rules.when: solids_present == true or fouling_tendency in ['high','severe'] or wax_or_asphaltenes_present == true
small_droplet_removal_required == true and fouling_tendency in ['none','low'] and high_liquid_loading == false

recommend_when: inlet device does not ensure uniform flow
effective droplet-settling length must be established

initialization.note: Example starting value only. Not a mandatory API ratio.

mandatory_disclaimer: Preliminary process-sizing recommendation based on API RP 12J. Final vessel geometry, mechanical design, internals performance, nozzle arrangement, pressure drop, relief design and fabrication details require qualified process, mechanical and technology-supplier review.

assumption_governance.purpose: Prevent hidden defaults and help the user understand why each value exists, how it affects preliminary sizing, and who must confirm it.

api_requirement_or_recommendation.meaning: A requirement, recommendation, equation, limit or design principle taken from the stated API basis.

api_typical_value.meaning: A typical or initial value shown by the API source. It is not automatically a universal mandatory value.

company_configurable_default.meaning: A controlled organizational default used to start an iteration when the API source does not prescribe one universal value.

project_process_input.meaning: A value supplied by the process design basis, heat and material balance, process simulation, project specification or approved datasheet.

worked_example_assumption.meaning: A synthetic demonstration value used only to show the calculation flow.

vendor_required.meaning: A value that must ultimately be confirmed by the separator internals technology supplier.

calculated.meaning: A value produced by a formula or geometry calculation.

engineering_selection.meaning: A value selected by a qualified engineer after evaluating trade-offs and constraints.

worked_examples.title: Synthetic horizontal gas-oil-water separator
worked_examples.objective: Show how process inputs, API-based limits, engineering assumptions and vendor-dependent values interact to produce a preliminary vessel size and internals recommendation.

relevant_sections: Section 5.2 Horizontal Two-phase and Three-phase Separator Specifications

assumption_explanations.intention: Defines whether the vessel must separate gas, oil and water.
assumption_explanations.importance: It controls orientation logic, liquid-liquid settling checks, level architecture, outlet arrangement and internal configuration.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Three-phase service usually adds interface-control volume and droplet-settling length compared with a two-phase scrubber.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: The app may omit the water section, interface level and one of the liquid outlets.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Require the user to select the phase system before any sizing calculation is enabled.

assumption_explanations.intention: Establishes the operating condition at which gas density and volumetric flow must be evaluated.
assumption_explanations.importance: Gas capacity is based on actual volumetric flow and density at vessel conditions, not standard flow alone.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: For the same gas mass flow, higher operating gas density normally reduces actual gas volume and gas-area demand.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Using standard-condition gas properties can materially oversize or undersize the gas section.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Obtain pressure from the approved process design case and calculate properties at that condition.

assumption_explanations.intention: Defines the temperature for density, viscosity and interfacial-property evaluation.
assumption_explanations.importance: Temperature can change gas volume, liquid viscosity, surface tension and droplet-settling performance.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Higher liquid viscosity generally reduces droplet terminal velocity and increases required effective separation length.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: The geometry may pass with incorrect fluid properties but fail under the real operating case.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Evaluate design, normal and minimum cases using case-specific properties.

assumption_explanations.intention: Quantifies the gas load entering the vessel.
assumption_explanations.importance: Gas load drives required gas-flow area, mist-eliminator area and gas outlet size.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Increasing gas flow normally increases vessel diameter or requires higher-capacity internals.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Understated peak gas flow creates liquid carryover and excessive nozzle velocity.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Use the governing design flow and separately check normal and minimum turndown cases.

assumption_explanations.intention: Quantifies the hydrocarbon-liquid load.
assumption_explanations.importance: Oil flow affects liquid velocity, retention volume, oil outlet size and water-droplet settling through oil.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Increasing oil flow generally increases liquid-section area, level volume or vessel length.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: The vessel may have inadequate residence time or oil outlet capacity.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Use design flow for sizing and minimum flow for interface-control operability checks.

assumption_explanations.intention: Quantifies the aqueous-phase load.
assumption_explanations.importance: Water flow affects interface level, water-section area, oil-droplet rising length and water outlet size.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Increasing water flow increases required water volume and may increase vessel diameter or length.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Water carryover into oil or oil carryover into water may exceed downstream limits.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Include normal, maximum water and upset-water cases where applicable.

assumption_explanations.intention: Converts gas mass flow to actual volume and enters the Souders-Brown relationship.
assumption_explanations.importance: It strongly influences gas capacity, allowable velocity and nozzle momentum.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Lower gas density usually increases actual gas volume and can increase gas-area demand.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Incorrect gas density can dominate the vessel-diameter error.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Use a validated property package at each operating pressure and temperature.

assumption_explanations.intention: Defines the light-liquid density for gas separation and the continuous-phase density for water settling.
assumption_explanations.importance: Density difference affects allowable gas velocity and droplet terminal velocity.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: A smaller density difference reduces separation driving force and increases required area or length.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: The app may overstate separation performance.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Use the lightest credible hydrocarbon density for gas-capacity screening where required.

assumption_explanations.intention: Defines the heavy-phase density.
assumption_explanations.importance: The oil-water density difference is the principal gravity-driving force for liquid-liquid separation.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: A smaller oil-water density difference increases settling and rising length.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Emulsion-prone or near-density services can be seriously undersized.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Use the minimum credible density difference across the operating envelope.

assumption_explanations.intention: Represents resistance to water-droplet movement through the oil phase.
assumption_explanations.importance: Viscosity directly affects droplet Reynolds number and terminal velocity.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Higher oil viscosity reduces water-droplet settling velocity and increases required separation length.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Cold, heavy or waxy oil service may be substantially undersized.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Use the highest credible oil viscosity for water-in-oil separation checks.

assumption_explanations.intention: Represents resistance to oil-droplet rise through the water phase.
assumption_explanations.importance: It affects the required oil-removal length in the water compartment.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Higher water viscosity increases the required effective separation length.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: The water outlet may contain more oil than expected.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Use case-specific viscosity and include contaminants where they materially change rheology.

assumption_explanations.intention: Characterizes droplet formation, coalescence tendency and emulsion behavior.
assumption_explanations.importance: Low interfacial tension can make small droplets more stable and reduce practical separation performance.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Lower interfacial tension may require conservative droplet targets, coalescing internals or more separation length.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: A gravity-only design may be recommended for a stable emulsion that requires special treatment.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Flag low-interfacial-tension service for process testing or technology-supplier review.

assumption_explanations.intention: Defines the smallest water droplet that the oil section is expected to remove.
assumption_explanations.importance: It converts an outlet-quality expectation into a gravity-settling design criterion.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Smaller target droplets have lower terminal velocity and require more effective separation length.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Selecting an easy large-droplet target may produce unacceptable water in oil.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Link the target to a stated outlet-quality requirement and downstream tolerance.

assumption_explanations.intention: Defines the smallest oil droplet expected to rise out of the water phase.
assumption_explanations.importance: It governs the required water-compartment separation length.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Smaller oil droplets increase required effective separation length.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: The produced-water outlet may fail downstream oil-in-water limits.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Require the user to state the water outlet quality or select an approved project droplet target.

assumption_explanations.intention: Provides a preliminary liquid inventory check in addition to droplet-settling calculations.
assumption_explanations.importance: Retention time affects controllability, surge tolerance and the time available for disengagement.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Longer retention time increases required liquid volume and usually vessel length or diameter.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: A universal retention time can overdesign one service and underdesign another.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Treat retention time as project-specific and do not use it as a substitute for droplet-settling checks.

assumption_explanations.intention: Provides a starting geometry for iterative horizontal-vessel sizing.
assumption_explanations.importance: It balances diameter, length, plot space, internals arrangement and fabrication economics.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: A larger ratio tends to reduce diameter but increases footprint and separation travel length.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Treating the initial ratio as mandatory can prevent the app from finding a better geometry.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Use 4.0 only as an initial trial and iterate standard diameter-length combinations.

assumption_explanations.intention: Provides gas-flow area, liquid cross-sectional area, level spacing and internal clearances.
assumption_explanations.importance: Diameter is usually the highest-leverage geometry variable because it affects gas and liquid capacity simultaneously.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Increasing diameter lowers gas and liquid velocities and increases level volume, but raises vessel weight and cost.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: A gas-only diameter may fail liquid separation, while excessive diameter can waste capital.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Select the smallest standard diameter that passes every applicable criterion.

assumption_explanations.intention: Provides retention volume, droplet travel length and space for inlet, baffle, mist and outlet zones.
assumption_explanations.importance: Length frequently governs three-phase and slug-handling services.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Increasing length increases retention and effective separation distance without increasing diameter.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Using total tangent length as effective separation length can overstate separation performance.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Separate total tangent length from usable effective separation length in the app.

assumption_explanations.intention: Represents the usable gravity-separation distance after deducting inlet, baffle, weir, mist and outlet zones.
assumption_explanations.importance: Droplet-settling models must compare required length with usable length, not overall vessel length.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: A shorter effective length can make an apparently adequate vessel fail liquid-liquid separation.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: The app may credit space occupied by internals as active separation volume.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Calculate this value from the selected internal arrangement and nozzle locations.

assumption_explanations.intention: Converts fluid density difference into allowable gas velocity.
assumption_explanations.importance: It directly controls gas-area demand and therefore can control vessel diameter.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: A higher K-factor reduces required gas area, but may reduce separation margin.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Using an optimistic K-factor without matching internals can cause liquid carryover.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Select K from the actual orientation and demisting arrangement and apply service derating where needed.

assumption_explanations.intention: Estimates the drainage head needed for the mist-eliminator drainpipe.
assumption_explanations.importance: Insufficient drainage head can flood the mist eliminator and sharply reduce performance.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Higher pressure drop increases required LSH-to-mist spacing and may increase vessel height or diameter.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: The selected mist element may flood at design rate.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Replace the example value with vendor pressure-drop data before finalizing geometry.

assumption_explanations.intention: Balances flow redistribution against pressure drop through the baffle.
assumption_explanations.importance: Uniform flow protects effective separation length and reduces short-circuiting.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Too little open area raises pressure drop; too much may provide weak redistribution.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Poor distribution can invalidate the ideal droplet-settling calculation.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Use the stated range for preliminary design and obtain detailed hydraulic or CFD review for critical service.

assumption_explanations.intention: Provides minimum physical separation between control, alarm and trip levels.
assumption_explanations.importance: It supports reliable instrumentation, operator response and control stability.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Larger required spacing increases liquid inventory and can reduce gas area in a horizontal vessel.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: Closely spaced levels may cause nuisance alarms, trips or poor control.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Apply the greater of the minimum physical spacing and the spacing needed for the required control time.

assumption_explanations.intention: Ensures that each level interval contains sufficient operating volume.
assumption_explanations.importance: Time-based volume prevents a geometrically adequate spacing from being operationally too small.
assumption_explanations.sizing_effect: Higher flow increases required volume and may increase spacing, length or diameter.
assumption_explanations.risk_if_wrong: A vessel can satisfy 150 mm spacing but still have inadequate response time at high flow.
assumption_explanations.recommendation: Check both the distance criterion and the time-volume criterion.

decision_trace.logic: Three-phase gas-oil-water separation requires liquid-liquid interface area, effective settling length and two liquid outlets.
General service with no solids and moderate fouling requires initial bulk separation and flow distribution.

decision_trace.decision: Select horizontal-flow vane pack without pockets
decision_trace.logic: Moderate fouling favors a more open demister than knitted mesh; the selected K-factor is used only for preliminary gas-area screening.

decision_trace.decision: Start with 1.5 m ID and 6.0 m tangent length
decision_trace.logic: The 4.0 initial L/D trial provides a practical first geometry for iteration.

gas_capacity.interpretation: Gas capacity does not govern this selected geometry.

bulk_liquid_velocity.interpretation: The actual velocity is near the conservative lower end of the preliminary range.

retention_volume.interpretation: This is a project-assumption check and does not replace droplet-settling calculations.

oil_outlet_nozzle.recommendation: Provide a vortex breaker and verify pump-suction criteria when applicable.

water_outlet_nozzle.recommendation: Provide a vortex breaker and verify self-venting or carry-under risk.

recommendations.message: Replace all synthetic process inputs with approved design, normal and minimum operating cases.
Confirm inlet-device and mist-eliminator performance, dimensions, pressure drop and drainage with the technology supplier.
Confirm the 350 micrometre water-droplet and 150 micrometre oil-droplet targets against required outlet quality.
Verify effective separation length after finalizing the baffle, weir, nozzle and mist-eliminator arrangement.
Perform sensitivity cases for maximum gas rate, maximum water rate, minimum oil-water density difference and maximum oil viscosity.
The selected 1.5 m by 6.0 m geometry is a preliminary process-screening result, not a mechanically designed pressure vessel.

ui_explanation_and_recommendation_logic.governing_criterion_message_template: {criterion} governs because its required value is closest to the available capacity.
ui_explanation_and_recommendation_logic.non_governing_criterion_message_template: {criterion} does not govern, but it remains a mandatory pass check.
ui_explanation_and_recommendation_logic.override_message_template: The user changed {parameter_id} from {original_value} to {new_value}. The original value and justification remain in the audit record.
